title: Hand-made resources in the running Anthus deployments are imported, not replaced
description:
Design and dry-run only until Ryan has seen each change set. Never create, change or import in the Anthus account without his go-ahead.

```gherkin
Feature: Existing resources join the pipeline in place

  Scenario: A hand-made zone, role or provider is imported
    Given a resource that was made by hand and is in use
    When the pipeline first manages it
    Then the change set shows Import and no Add, Modify or Remove of that resource
    And the resource has DeletionPolicy and UpdateReplacePolicy Retain
    And for a Route 53 zone the name servers are the same before and after

  Scenario: Nothing is imported until a person has seen the change set
    Given an import of a production resource
    Then the first run stops at the change set for approval
```

comments.text:
# Dry-run plan: adopt the Anthus account's hand-made resources (read-only research; nothing applied)

Read-only calls with the Anthus profile, 2026-11-11. No ids or addresses recorded here.

| Resource | Records | Alias records | Tags | Private/VPC | Query logging | DNSSEC | Referenced by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| anth.us | 100 | 34 | none | no | none | not signing | HostedZoneId parameter of papyrus-edge-shipped-console, -machines-on-machines-console, -tactus, -tactus-site (tactus is ROLLBACK_COMPLETE), papyrus-newsletter-sending-operators and -shipped |
| apyr.us | 27 | 8 | none | no | none | not signing | no stack |
| pilobol.us | 15 | 4 | none | no | none | not signing | no stack |
| distinctive-mark.com | 14 | 4 | none | no | none | not signing | papyrus-newsletter-sending-distinctive |
| ryanalynporter.com | 10 | 0 | none | no | none | not signing | no stack |
The account has no health checks and no reusable delegation sets. References are by value (a parameter), never an import or export, so importing a zone (which keeps its id) cannot break the dependent stacks. No Papyrus template defines these zones, so there is no collision; `infra/account/stacks/dns.yaml` is the only HostedZone template.

## The budget: do NOT import with the current template
`papyrus-amplify-monthly` is a 72.78 USD monthly cost budget filtered to Service = AWS Amplify, one notification (ACTUAL > 100%), one subscriber of type SNS (not EMAIL), no tags, no actions, in no stack. `infra/account/stacks/budget.yaml` has a 200 limit, no cost filter, three notifications and EMAIL subscribers; `BudgetName` and `NotificationsWithSubscribers` are create-only, so importing would show a Replace and the deployer would refuse it. Options: (a) a variant template for this budget (Service filter, 72.78, one notification, the existing SNS topic as a plain parameter); (b) leave it hand-made. Recommendation: (b) for now: `amplify-cost-check.mjs` reads it by name and the amount is probably meant to change. No alert-address SSM parameter is needed for it.

## Per-zone stacks.json block (repeat per zone)
```json
{
  "name": "papyrus-dns-<domain-with-hyphens>",
  "template": "papyrus:infra/account/stacks/dns.yaml",
  "enabled": false,
  "reason": "waiting for the go-ahead",
  "parameters": {"DomainName": "<domain>", "ZoneComment": "<live comment, verbatim>"},
  "import": {"logicalId": "HostedZone", "resourceType": "AWS::Route53::HostedZone",
             "lookup": {"kind": "hostedZoneByName", "name": "<domain>"}, "identifierKey": "Id"},
  "checks": [{"kind": "nameservers", "zone": "<domain>", "expectedFile": "expected-nameservers.json"}]
}
```
The live comment must match exactly (the follow-up update applies it). `expected-nameservers.json` holds each zone's four live name servers, read with `aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id <zone-id> --query 'DelegationSet.NameServers'` and compared with `dig NS <domain> +short`. Save the "before" output; after the import the set must be identical.

## What the IMPORT change set must show
Exactly one change: Action Import on `HostedZone` (`AWS::Route53::HostedZone`). Outputs are stripped from the import template by the deployer and return in the follow-up update, which should be a no-op or a Modify of the comment only (it may add `aws:cloudformation:*` tags, harmless). Red flags, stop and do not execute: any action other than Import; a Replace or Remove of the zone; a changed Name or comment; a second zone for the same name; any record-set change. Records are never managed by the imported zone resource (including anth.us's 34 alias records).

## Rollback
`DeletionPolicy` and `UpdateReplacePolicy` are Retain. A failed or doubtful import leaves the zone, its records and name servers untouched. After success, delete the stack with `--retain-resources` to undo.

## Order
1. ryanalynporter.com (10 records, no aliases, no references: the rehearsal). 2. apyr.us. 3. pilobol.us. 4. distinctive-mark.com. 5. anth.us last, with the rehearsal results in hand.

## Approval and unknowns
Ryan reads each dry-run change set and says go ahead per zone or for the batch after the rehearsal; nothing is needed in GitHub; `enabled` flips to true only after that. Unknowns: whether the Anthus pipeline roles allow Route 53 import (the Anthus account would use its own baseline, not yet seeded there); whether anything outside CloudFormation edits records during the window; the budget's SNS topic and subscribers.

Note on mechanism: the Anthus account uses the older papyrus-pipeline-approver and papyrus-stack-pipeline stacks, not the account baseline. Using the account pipeline there means seeding the baseline in the Anthus account first (one documented apply by a person, with a prefix such as papyrus and the Papyrus repository), or adding the import ability to the existing role-stack-deploy path. That choice is Ryan's; nothing is applied.
